summary: The U.S. Space Force expects to spend an additional $17 billion on launch capabilities amid soaring demand, as the service also conducted its first "live fly" orbital dogfighting exercise in space and selected Texas as the preferred site for its third Deep Space Advanced Radar Capability facility. In civil space developments, NASA added Relativity Space’s Terran R rocket to its Launch Services Contract, requested proposals to accelerate lunar surface technologies, and named two Artemis II crew members to its Emeritus Program following their retirement from active flight duty. On Mars, NASA's Curiosity rover logged its 5,000th Martian day of operations, while scientific discoveries elsewhere included James Webb Space Telescope observations showing changing rings around the asteroid Chariklo and Chandra X-ray Observatory data revealing mysterious hypersoft X-ray sources. Commercial investments surged as rocket developer Stoke Space raised $1 billion to advance its fully reusable launch vehicle, and European firm The Exploration Company secured $450 million in Series C funding. Internationally, the United Kingdom announced a $10.6 billion, four-year space spending plan focused heavily on defense, while commercial operator Eutelsat selected Infinite Orbits for a geostationary satellite life-extension mission. Looking ahead, industry observers should watch for Stoke Space's planned early 2027 debut launch of its fully reusable rocket.
